question: The seven years of war in the 18th century was fought between Britain and ________.
solution:
The Correct answer is France

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****The Seven Years’ War**, also known as the **French and Indian War**, was a global conflict fought primarily between **Great Britain** (supported by Prussia) and **France** (backed by Spain, Saxony, Sweden, and Russia) from 1756 to 1763. This war had significant implications for both Europe and the Americas. 

__
 
• **Background**__:

 __
 
• The Seven Years’ War emerged from ongoing tensions between European powers after the War of the Austrian Succession (which ended in 1748).
 
• Colonial disputes between Britain and France in North America escalated, leading to the outbreak of the French and Indian War in 1754.
 
• Traditional alliances shifted during the so-called 1756 Diplomatic Revolution: Prussia allied with Britain.
 
• Austria signed a treaty with France, ending the long-running French–Habsburg rivalry.
 
 
 
• **Participants**__:
 __
 
• Great Britain, primarily supported by Prussia.
 
• France, backed by Spain, Saxony, Sweden, and Russia.
 
 
 
• **Outcomes**__:
 __
 
• France ceded its North American possessions east of the Mississippi River, Canada, and several Caribbean islands to Britain.
 
• Spain ceded Florida to Britain in exchange for the return of Havana and Manila.
 
• The war concluded with the **1763 Treaty of Paris**__.
